questions.title: What to do if an animal moves your golf ball
questions.question: A squirrel comes onto the course and moves your golf ball from where it was sitting. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the squirrel left it
Put the ball back where it was, with no penalty
Add one shot and drop the ball anywhere nearby
Skip this hole and go to the next one

questions.explanation: If an animal like a squirrel moves your ball, you put your ball back where it was. You do not get a penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: An extra shot added to your score for breaking a rule
To put the ball back in the same spot it was before
Something not part of your game, like an animal or the wind, that changes your ball

questions.teachingTip: You can ask the child to show you where they would put the ball back if an animal moved it, so they understand 'replace.'
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you have to play the ball where the animal left it.
Thinking you get a penalty shot for the animal's action.

questions.title: What to do if your ball is moved by a squirrel
questions.question: A squirrel runs onto the course and moves your ball from where it was resting. What is the correct action under the Rules?

choices.text: Play the ball from where the squirrel left it
Replace the ball as close as possible to its original spot, with no penalty
Add a penalty stroke and drop the ball
Skip the hole and move to the next one

questions.explanation: If an outside influence, such as a squirrel, moves your ball at rest, you must replace it as close as possible to its original spot with no penalty.
